full_details: At ten, at the stage door, George Bryan asked which of two readings was current. Eleven lines of the comedy had been asked for in a fair copy. You started to explain, and you saw he needed a choice. You chose the shorter reading and marked the sheet with a cross. He was gone before you could add a second improvement. You wrote the choice down and did not write the improvement. In the afternoon you played the comedy again. At home the parish clerk had been round with a precept from Crosby Place, to be read in church on Sunday next: no blue starch in ruffs. He did not stay. Mistress Ansell had it by heart before supper. She said starch is good wheat boiled to vanity, and blue is vanity dyed. Alse has one band starched blue, bought at Whitsun last, and she sat very still. You asked whether the Mayor had found the root of the dearth in our collars. Mistress Ansell said you may laugh, that he is a hard man and right about ruffs. Alse may wash the band white. At the table the loaf was a finger and a half short, and a penny. Under Prices you wrote: blew starch, forbid; the loaf, two fingers.
one_sentence: You chose the shorter reading for Bryan, played the comedy again, and heard the Mayor's precept against blue starch at supper.
title: A cross on the shorter reading, and blue starch
